contents.name: §2, isolated massive shell, local interpolators, and compact momentum packets
contents.support: The review states the positive-mass shell and local-interpolation hypotheses, defines the one-particle projection and translation-smoothed operators, and uses compact momentum supports. Its stability hypothesis is more general than an isolated mass gap; the item states the selected isolated-shell case explicitly.

contents.name: §2, equations (2.4)–(2.5): derivative decay and Cook limits
contents.support: The source differentiates Haag–Ruelle approximants and explains that integrable norm decay gives strong limits. Its locality and stability estimates are construction inputs; the item proves the abstract Hilbert-space Cook implication in full.

contents.name: §1 and §2, equations (2.5)–(2.7) and Theorem 1: ranges of wave maps
contents.support: The source maps Fock space isometrically onto incoming and outgoing scattering subspaces and separates equality of those subspaces from full asymptotic completeness.

sources.title: Klaus Fredenhagen, Quantum Field Theory, lecture notes, Wintersemester 2009/10 and Sommersemester 2010
sources.locator: Complete 143-page lecture notes; Chapter IV §3, PDF pp. 82–85, especially Theorems IV.1 and IV.2.

contents.name: Chapter IV §3, Theorem IV.1: almost-local generators and velocity support
contents.support: The notes state an upper mass gap, construct almost-local one-particle generators, define velocity support as p/omega(p), and use disjoint velocity supports. Their almost-local approximation is on a common dense domain; the item records both bounded norm and common-domain versions.

contents.name: Chapter IV §3, Theorem IV.2: two-particle limits and Fock inner products
contents.support: The source states convergence and the bosonic two-particle inner product, then says the complete proof is in the literature. The item supplies a complete conditional proof of the Hilbert-valued integrable-derivative theorem and leaves Fock inner-product convergence as a separate hypothesis.

contents.name: Chapter IV §3, Theorem IV.2 and following discussion: wave-map ranges
contents.support: The notes identify isometric wave maps and state that their unitarity does not follow from Haag–Ruelle convergence; asymptotic completeness is a separate condition.

sources.title: Detlev Buchholz and Wojciech Dybalski, Scattering in relativistic quantum field theory: basic concepts, tools, and results
sources.locator: Complete 16-page PDF; §1, PDF pp. 2–3, and §2, PDF pp. 4–5.

contents.name: §1–2: wave maps have ranges in the physical Hilbert space
contents.support: The review distinguishes isometric maps into scattering subspaces from range equality and full completeness. The finite-dimensional counterexample itself is constructed and computed locally.
